3,GLOBAL,Whole Mass,General principles / participation,,,"The new Code of Rubrics was ordered to be observed from 1 January 1961. Earlier general rubrics, the 1955 simplification decree, and decrees/replies incompatible with the new Code ceased to have force; contrary statutes, privileges, indults and customs were revoked.","Mass by its nature requires all present to participate according to their proper role. Participation is first interior; it becomes more complete through exterior acts such as kneeling, standing, sitting, ceremonial gestures, responses, prayers and singing; sacramental Communion is identified as the complete form of active participation.","The faithful truly participate in the Eucharistic oblation, but not by performing the priest's visible sacrificial rite: the consecratory immolation is performed by the priest alone in the person of Christ. The faithful offer through the priest and, in a distinct sense, together with him by uniting praise, petition, expiation and thanksgiving to the priest's and Christ's intention.",,,,,"Oakeley explicitly states that although he tried to follow approved ceremonial rules, the work is not intended as authority on rubrical subjects.
• Oakeley distinguishes the Church’s printed preparation prayers from an absolute obligation to use every text, while insisting that the priest devote some time before Mass, according to circumstances, to vocal or mental prayer.
• Oakeley explicitly says the prescribed preparatory Psalms may be used with great profit not only by the priest but also by those who hear Mass when they have leisure for fuller preparation.
• He interprets Ps 83 as longing for God’s house and presence; Ps 84 as redemption; Ps 85 as mercy and proper disposition; Ps 115 as confidence/thanksgiving; and Ps 129 as intercession for the dead for whom the Sacrifice is offered.
• Oakeley explains pre-Mass handwashing as practical and symbolic purification, then reads the vestments as formation: amice/alb—purity; girdle—readiness/chastity; maniple—present sorrow and future joy; stole—immortality; chasuble/cross—Passion and bearing Christ’s yoke.",,,,,,,,,,"The introduction teaches that attending Mass is not passive: the faithful should offer themselves with Jesus in His Sacrifice, using the image of Mary and St John at Calvary.
• Chapter I visually teaches the sacristy, vestments, vesting prayers, sacred vessels, altar linens and a labeled altar diagram, giving the faithful a 'behind the scenes' preparation layer before the priest enters.
• Chapter II uses staircase diagrams to teach the major divisions of Mass and a progression of prayer and instruction toward the sacrificial/Communion climax; a second diagram distinguishes stages where the people speak to God and where God teaches through Scripture/Church."
4,GLOBAL-LOW,Low Mass,General Low-Mass participation framework,,,,"At Low Mass the use of a hand missal is specially praised, but the instruction expressly recognizes that not everyone has the same capacity or spiritual needs; meditation on Christ's mysteries and other devotions/prayers that differ externally from the rite but harmonize with it are legitimate methods of participation.
• Low-Mass participation may progress from private interior/exterior participation, to common prayers/songs, to liturgical dialogue. Four dialogue degrees are listed: simple responses; server parts; Ordinary; then Proper for advanced groups.",,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,
5,E01,Preparation,Entrance / procession,,,,,,"For Solemn Mass, O'Connell's suggested congregational ceremonial has all stand during the entrance procession until the sacred ministers salute the altar; at Low Community Mass the people stand as the celebrant enters.",,,,,,,,,"Lasance frames assistance at Mass by uniting oneself with the priest's offering and the four ends: adoration, satisfaction/reparation, thanksgiving and petition.",,St. Leonard explicitly permits different holy methods of hearing Mass; his 'third method' divides the Mass into four periods corresponding to four debts owed to God rather than requiring a word-for-word private prayer track.,"The priest's emergence from the sacristy is interpreted as Christ's Nativity/public manifestation; the underlying work presents the Mass as an epitome of Christ's whole life, not only His Passion.",,"At the start of 'Getting Ready' the book tells the faithful to be in their seat and waiting before the priest leaves the sacristy, then gives immediate posture cues as the priest approaches and begins Mass."
6,E02,Preparation,Asperges (when applicable),,,,,,"At the Asperges all stand, join in the chant, and sign themselves when sprinkled.",,,,,"At High Mass, faithful stand for the Asperges.",,,,,,,,,
7,E03,Preparation,Sign of the Cross / Judica me,The 1962 Ritus begins Low Mass at the foot of the altar with the sign of the Cross and preparatory prayers; exact omissions depend on the Mass/day.,"Rubrics 424–425: Judica, its antiphon, the Confiteor/absolution and related foot-of-altar prayers are the normal opening, with explicit omissions for processional-integrated Masses; Judica alone is omitted in Passiontide seasonal Masses and Requiem.",,,,"At Low Community Mass the people may kneel and say the opening prayers with the priest, or remain standing for a suitable entrance hymn/psalm or silent prayer; these options end before Introit/Kyrie as applicable.",,"Augustine treats bodily actions/posture as integral to liturgical action and discusses the Sign of the Cross as a sacramental gesture; he distinguishes standing, kneeling and sitting traditions.",Server makes the full Sign of the Cross deliberately; Britt gives exact hand placement and forehead–breast–left shoulder–right shoulder execution.,"Oakeley calls Judica a Psalm of preparation for the altar and explains the minister as answering in the name of the congregation. He adds that rapid ceremonial makes prior knowledge of the words/actions more—not less—important, because it lets the mind grasp the fitting thought immediately.",Low Mass: faithful ordinarily kneel throughout except at the Gospels. High Mass: kneel from the beginning until the Gloria.,,,,"Lasance supplies acts of adoration/contrition around opening prayers and Confiteor, but does not make them a mandatory synchronized private-prayer script.",Knox interprets Judica and the opening preparation as the Church separating herself from the profane world before approaching the altar; he immediately distinguishes this from the more personal Confiteor.,,,Foot of altar → Christ enters Gethsemane / prayer in the garden.,The chapter presents the foot-of-altar prayers as preparation before the priest ascends and explicitly connects Confiteor with sorrow for sin and intercession for the priest.

12,E08,Mass of Catechumens,Introit,,"Rubric 427 prescribes the Entrance antiphon with psalm verse and Gloria Patri, followed by repetition of the antiphon, subject to stated exceptions.",,"For sung Mass, trained faithful may sing the Proper; the Entrance antiphon may be extended with additional psalm verses during a longer entrance.",,At Solemn Mass the Introit is sung as the ministers enter; after the ministers salute the altar the people kneel unless they themselves are singing the Introit.,,,,"Oakeley calls the Introit the 'Entrance' upon Mass, treats the earlier foot prayers as introductory, and explains the antiphon/psalm material as giving the Mass its day/season character.",Low Mass: faithful ordinarily kneel throughout except at the Gospels. High Mass: kneel from the beginning until the Gloria.,Wynne explains Introit as 'entrance/beginning' and as a scriptural/psalm text expressing the sentiment of the Mass of the day.,O'Brien treats the Introit as giving the scope/key or dominant sentiment of the Mass of the day and traces its ceremonial history.,Guéranger explains that the Introit originally belonged to the choir during the entrance; later priestly recitation reflects the development of Low Mass and subsequent duplication at sung Mass.,"Lasance provides an Introit-associated devotional prayer/psalm, while explicitly saying the faithful need not say every supplied prayer.",Knox interprets the Introit as the point where the priest moves from preparatory hesitation into the liturgy of the day.,,The Introit at the Epistle side symbolizes the Presentation in the Temple; the surrounding ministers receive further symbolic identifications.,Introit → Christ receives a blow at the house of Annas.,
13,E09,Mass of Catechumens,Kyrie,,"Rubric 430 specifies the ninefold Kyrie: Kyrie three times, Christe three times, Kyrie three times.",,Kyrie is among the Ordinary chants the faithful are to be taught to sing; simpler Ordinary parts may be assigned to the people even if Gloria/Credo remain with the schola.,,"At Solemn Mass the people stand while singing Kyrie; if the ministers sit during the chant, the people may sit also. 14,E10,Mass of Catechumens,Gloria,,Rubrics 431–432 specify when Gloria is said or omitted; among the omissions are Masses with violet vestments and Masses of the Dead.,,"Gloria is included among the Ordinary parts that may be sung by all the faithful; if needed, it may remain with the schola while simpler Ordinary chants are sung by the people.",,At Solemn Mass the people stand for the sung Gloria but may sit when the ministers sit; at Low Community Mass they stand and recite Gloria with the priest after his intonation.,,,,"Oakeley treats the Gloria as the Angelic Hymn, a movement from the Kyrie's supplication into praise and thanksgiving. 15,E11,Mass of Catechumens,Collect(s),,,,,,The congregation normally stands for the Collect and responses; at most Masses in violet vestments and at Requiem Mass they kneel for Collects and Postcommunions.,,,,"Oremus is explained as an invitation to the people to join the priest in prayer; the plural expresses Mass as common worship, and 'Collect' gathers the needs and desires of the people into prayer.

16,E12,Mass of Catechumens,Epistle / Lesson,,Rubric 466 places the Epistle after the prayers with Deo gratias; in sung Masses rubric 473 removes from the celebrant what a subdeacon or lector proclaims by office.,,,,At Solemn Mass the faithful sit for Lessons/Epistle; at Low Community Mass they are seated while reading/listening to the Epistle.,,,"In Missa Cantata, a cleric may sing the Epistle; Britt also describes the acolyte's choreography around the book.",He treats the Epistle as the Church’s ancient scriptural instruction and interprets Deo gratias as the people’s thanksgiving for the gift of divine teaching.,"At High Mass, sit during the Epistle and remain seated through the intervening chant phase until the Gospel transition.",Wynne presents the Epistle as the scriptural reading that precedes the Gospel in the lay-facing Ordinary.,"O'Brien treats the Epistle as an ancient scriptural lesson preceding the Gospel, with roots in synagogue/early Christian reading and historical use of the ambo.",,Lasance gives scriptural/moral devotional material for 'At the Epistle' rather than a posture rule.,"Knox describes the Epistle as a relative relaxation in Low Mass: a letter read to the faithful, with less ceremonial tension than the surrounding prayers.",,The Epistle/interlection/Gospel-preparation complex is interpreted through the Flight into Egypt and return; this is tied to Dominican solemn choreography.,Epistle → Christ brought before Pilate.,Chapter V frames the Epistle as God the Father teaching through prophets and apostles and explicitly cues the learner to sit and listen.

18,E14,Mass of Catechumens,Alleluia / Tract,,Rubric 469 orders Gradual then Alleluia or Tract; this is part of the scriptural/chant sequence before the Gospel.,,,,"O'Connell groups Alleluia/Tract with the interlection chants: faithful sit while listening, but stand if they themselves sing them.",,,,,"At High Mass, sit during the Epistle and remain seated through the intervening chant phase until the Gospel transition.",,,"While the choir sings the intervening chant, Gospel preparation by ministers can already be underway; chant and preparation are not purely serial.",,,,,,

20,E16,Mass of Catechumens,Gospel preparation (Solemn),,,,,,,,,"For Solemn Mass the thurifer retrieves the censer after the Epistle; incense is blessed and the Gospel group forms with thurifer, acolytes, deacon and subdeacon.",,,,,"Guéranger explicitly connects the intervening chants with the time required for Gospel preparation: book, incense, Munda cor meum, blessing and procession.",,Knox interprets the movement to the Gospel side and the preparatory prayer over the lips/heart as a special preparation to proclaim the words of life.,,,Munda cor meum → Christ brought before Herod.,

23,E19,Mass of Catechumens,Three small Gospel crosses,The three small crosses are prescribed for the liturgical minister proclaiming the Gospel; this source does not create a universal lay rubric to imitate them.,,,,,"O'Connell explicitly directs the congregation at Solemn Mass to make the small sign of the Cross on forehead, lips, and breast at the Gospel.",,,"At each Gospel the ordinary server makes three small crosses on forehead, lips and breast with the thumb; Britt gives exact execution details.",Oakeley describes the three small crosses made by the priest at the Gospel as part of the ceremonial preparation/proclamation.,"Stand for the Gospel; at Solemn High Mass the posture cue is the Gospel sung by the deacon, not the celebrant's private reading.",,,Guéranger describes the Gospel proclaimer making crosses on book and forehead/lips/breast; his appended lay Ordinary also documents faithful use of the three small crosses.,,,,,,"The book explicitly shows the forehead, lips and breast Gospel crosses and tells the lay reader, 'You do it too.'"

This is valuable change evidence but not an active 1962 step.","At High Mass, Walsh's traditional lay track kneels from the Sanctus through Communion.",,"O'Brien documents the older Communion sequence with a server's second Confiteor, Misereatur/Indulgentiam, Ecce Agnus Dei and three Domine non sum dignus.",,,,,,,"Chapter X explicitly has the server say the Confiteor before the faithful approach, followed by Misereatur/Indulgentiam. This is excellent visual evidence for the pre-1962 state and must not be carried into the normative 1962 sequence."
66,E62,Communion of Faithful,Ecce Agnus Dei,"After the priest's Communion, when the faithful communicate, the rite proceeds to Ecce Agnus Dei and the Communion formulas without the old second Confiteor.","Rubric 503 orders Ecce Agnus Dei three times after the priest's Precious Blood, with the Confiteor/absolution omitted.",,,,"After the celebrant consumes the Precious Blood he prepares the ciborium/paten and, after the required genuflection, turns to say Ecce Agnus Dei; no second Confiteor intervenes.",,In Augustine's older sequence Ecce Agnus Dei follows the Confiteor/Misereatur/Indulgentiam complex.,,,"At High Mass, Walsh's traditional lay track kneels from the Sanctus through Communion.",,,,"Lasance provides Communion-oriented acts of faith, humility, thanksgiving and petition; these are devotional aids rather than rubrical lay actions.",,,,,At Ecce Agnus Dei the communicant is explicitly told to look at Our Lord in the Host.
67,E63,Communion of Faithful,Faithful Domine non sum dignus,Domine non sum dignus is said three times in preparation for Communion of the faithful.,Rubric 503 orders Domine non sum dignus three times before distribution of Communion.,,The faithful may recite the triple Domine non sum dignus with the celebrant before receiving Communion.,,O'Connell says Ecce Agnus Dei is followed by Domine non sum dignus three times; the entire prayer is aloud and communicants may say it aloud with the priest.,,Augustine's older sequence gives three Domine non sum dignus immediately before Communion.,The server strikes his breast at Domine non sum dignus only when those words immediately precede his own Communion.,,"At High Mass, Walsh's traditional lay track kneels from the Sanctus through Communion.",,,,"Lasance provides Communion-oriented acts of faith, humility, thanksgiving and petition; these are devotional aids rather than rubrical lay actions.",,,,,The communicants' triple Domine non sum dignus is explained as telling Jesus that they want Him to come to them.
68,E64,Communion of Faithful,Distribution of Holy Communion,Communion of the faithful follows the priest's Communion and precedes the ablutions.,"Rubrics 502–503: the proper time for Communion of the faithful is during Mass after the celebrant's Communion; after the Precious Blood and omission of Confiteor/absolution, Communion is distributed immediately after Ecce Agnus Dei / triple Domine non sum dignus.",,"The instruction calls sacramental reception the complete form of active participation, while still recognizing authentic interior and exterior participation by those who do not communicate.","It is especially fitting that the faithful receive Communion after the priest, and reception of Hosts consecrated at the same Mass is commended; reasonable pastoral exceptions can exist.",O'Connell treats Communion of the faithful as following the priest's Communion sequence; Community Mass guidance has communicants approach promptly at the warning bell and recite the triple Dnsd.,,,,,"At High Mass, Walsh's traditional lay track kneels from the Sanctus through Communion.",Wynne separately describes distribution of Holy Communion to the faithful after the priest's Communion.,O'Brien gives historical treatment of Communion practice and reception under the species.,Guéranger places Communion of faithful after priest's reception of Precious Blood and before ablutions.,"Lasance provides Communion-oriented acts of faith, humility, thanksgiving and petition; these are devotional aids rather than rubrical lay actions.",,"From Communion to the end of Mass, St. Leonard assigns petition/impetration, urging confidence in asking for great spiritual and temporal graces.",,Communion → Christ is buried.,"Chapter X gives visual reception mechanics: approach reverently, remain still at the rail, open the mouth, extend the tongue, and wait until the Host has been placed before closing the mouth; a right-way/wrong-way panel reinforces the instructions.
• After reception the book says to return reverently, consume the Host as soon as possible, and make a real thanksgiving: tell Jesus you are glad to have Him as guest and ask Him to stay with you always."
69,E65,Communion / Ablutions,Ablutions / purification,"After Communion and any distribution to the faithful, the priest performs the prescribed ablutions/purifications.",,,,,"After Communion, O'Connell says those who have not communicated may sit during the ablutions until the Postcommunion greeting.",,,"Britt gives two-server ablution choreography: wine/water are brought, Missal is transferred back, and servers return to position.",The ablutions are explained first by their practical purpose—ensuring reception of any remaining Sacred Species/fragments—and then by their accompanying prayers for interior purity and the enduring fruit of Communion.,"After Communion, sit while the priest purifies and covers the chalice.","Wynne describes ablutions as first rinsing the chalice with wine, then wine and water over the priest's fingers.",,,"Lasance provides Communion-oriented acts of faith, humility, thanksgiving and petition; these are devotional aids rather than rubrical lay actions.",,,Post-Communion movement toward the Epistle side and the emptied chalice symbolize the Resurrection and empty tomb.,Ablution → Christ is embalmed.,"Chapter XI uses the priest’s ablution prayers to teach a simple personal post-Communion method: ask Jesus to stay with you, bless you, and keep you from every kind of sin."
70,E66,Conclusion,Communion antiphon,In sung Mass the Communion antiphon is sung by the choir; it can overlap the ministerial Communion sequence depending on form.,Rubric 504 governs the Communion antiphon after the Canon and the intervening Communion rite.,,"When Communion is given to the faithful at sung Mass, the Communion antiphon should begin while the priest is distributing Communion; it may be prolonged with psalm verses and followed by another suitable Latin piece when distribution is lengthy.",,O'Connell says that when communicants are present the Communion antiphon is sung during distribution and may be prolonged with psalm verses; if none communicate it is sung while the celebrant receives.,,,,Oakeley treats the Communion as a short chant/text after the Communion of the faithful and as an abbreviated remnant of older psalmody; it normally bears on the feast or supplies an edifying Eucharistic sentiment.,"After Communion, sit while the priest purifies and covers the chalice.",,,,,,,,,It treats the Communion antiphon as one of the Church’s thanksgiving prayers and explains its historical link to a psalm formerly sung while the people went to Communion.
71,E67,Conclusion,Postcommunion,Postcommunion prayer(s) follow the Communion antiphon/ablutions and are said or sung according to form.,"Rubric 505 says Postcommunions follow the same number, manner and order as the prayers at the beginning of Mass; rubric 506 adds the Prayer over the People on specified Lenten/Passion ferias.",,,,Faithful stand for Dominus vobiscum/Postcommunion and respond; at violet/Requiem Masses they kneel.,,,,"Oakeley contrasts the three prayer families: the Collect seeks a blessing, the Secret refers to the Sacrifice about to be offered, and the Postcommunion concerns the fruits of Communion/Sacrifice in the soul.",Stand for the final prayers / concluding phase before the blessing.,,,,,,,Postcommunion is linked to Christ's post-Resurrection consolation of His Mother.,After Communion / Postcommunion → Resurrection and post-Resurrection consolations.,"The Postcommunion is presented as the principal official thanksgiving prayer after Communion, structurally corresponding to the Collect and Secret and prayed on behalf of the whole Church."
72,E68,Conclusion,Dismissal — Ite / Benedicamus / Requiescant,"The concluding formula depends on the Mass: Ite missa est, Benedicamus Domino, or Requiescant in pace as rubrically applicable.",Rubric 507: normally Ite missa est / Deo gratias; Benedicamus Domino where Mass is followed by a procession; Requiescant in pace / Amen in Masses of the Dead; Easter-octave seasonal Masses add double Alleluia.,,,,"The congregation answers the dismissal: Deo gratias to Ite missa est, Amen to Requiescant in pace.",,,,"He interprets the dismissal as a transition from contemplation to action: the time of contemplation is over, the time of action has come; the worshipper is sent back to work carrying what has been seen and received.",Stand for the final prayers / concluding phase before the blessing.,,,,,Knox treats Ite missa est as the signal that the gathered liturgical community disperses and each communicant returns to personal thanksgiving and ordinary life.,,Ite missa est symbolizes Christ's missionary commission sending the Apostles to teach the nations.,Dismissal / final Dominus vobiscum → Christ's commission / Ascension sequence in the devotional schema.,Chapter XII teaches the final rites as 'last-minute orders': the dismissal sends the faithful forth after offering the Sacrifice and receiving Communion.
73,E69,Conclusion,Placeat / final blessing,The blessing is not given in every case; the Ritus states the relevant exceptions in the final rites.,Rubric 508: the blessing follows Placeat and is omitted only when Benedicamus Domino or Requiescant in pace has been used.,,The organ is to remain silent while the celebrant gives the blessing at the end of Mass.,,"O'Connell directs the people to kneel for the blessing, sign themselves, answer Amen, then stand. If Benedicamus Domino is used there is no blessing and they remain standing.",,,,"Although Oakeley treats Ite missa est as ending the Mass in the strict sense, he says devout persons remain if possible until the priest leaves the altar so as not to miss the blessing.",Kneel for the final blessing.,Wynne places the final blessing before the Last Gospel in the concluding sequence.,,,,,,The Placeat/final blessing is associated with Christ's commissioning of Peter/Apostles and blessing of the faithful.,Priestly blessing → Pentecost / grace flowing from Christ's Passion in the reproduced method.,"It interprets the final blessing as strength to carry Christ into ordinary life through hard work, kindness, good example and doing what God wants."
74,E70,Conclusion,Last Gospel,"The normal Last Gospel is John 1:1–14, with restricted 1962 omissions/exceptions; the celebrant genuflects at Et Verbum caro factum est.","Rubrics 509–510: the normal Last Gospel is John 1; Palm Sunday retains a special proper Last Gospel when Mass does not follow the palms, and the Last Gospel is completely omitted in a restricted set of cases.",,,,O'Connell directs all to stand for the Last Gospel and genuflect with the priest at Et Verbum caro factum est; Low Community Mass likewise remains standing as the priest leaves.,,,Older Britt material includes the broader pre-1962 proper-Last-Gospel system and server choreography; this must not control 1962 exceptions.,"Oakeley records the genuflection at Et Verbum caro factum est in the Last Gospel and interprets it as reverence for the Incarnation.
• Oakeley records the Last Gospel and explains the genuflection at Et Verbum caro factum est as honouring the Incarnation.",Stand for the Last Gospel and genuflect at Et Verbum caro factum est.,"Wynne places the Last Gospel at the conclusion and reflects the older, broader proper-Last-Gospel system of his period.",O'Brien discusses the Last Gospel as a later addition to the Mass and its historical practice.,Guéranger explains the Last Gospel and its devotional/theological role in the historical Roman Mass.,,,,,,"The Last Gospel is used catechetically as a final reminder of what has been taught, so that the faithful can carry Christ and the Church’s instruction into the world."
75,E71,Conclusion,Departure / post-Mass prayers,,,,,"After Mass, a communicant's duty of thanksgiving is not thereby finished; personal thanksgiving after the liturgical action remains fitting.",,,,,,,,,,Lasance's framework naturally continues into thanksgiving after Mass; the four ends remain devotional orientation rather than a rubric.,,St. Leonard recommends thanksgiving after Mass; his method is intentionally flexible and says the worshipper need not cling to exact supplied words.,"The priest's return to the sacristy symbolizes the Ascension, completing St. Vincent's thirty-part life-of-Christ schema.",,The book distinguishes the short thanksgiving prayers within Mass from private thanksgiving afterward and says the faithful are expected to remain in church after Mass and make a private thanksgiving whenever they can.
